chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"If the deceased leaves two brothers, they are brothers with the deceased and they exclude the mother [from receiving one-third], and if there is only one, he does not exclude the mother." And he said, "If there are four sisters, they exclude the mother from receiving one-third, because they are in the position of the two brothers, and if there are three, they do not exclude her."
ai.seo_question: How many siblings are required to exclude the mother from her one-third inheritance share in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific numerical thresholds for the exclusion (*hijb*) of the mother from her one-third share (*sahm al-thaluth*) by full siblings. It establishes that two full brothers or four full sisters trigger this exclusion, whereas a single brother or three sisters do not, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential interpretation of sibling competition with the mother. This ruling is derived from the interplay between the Quranic verse and the Prophetic explanation regarding the division of the estate when parents and siblings coexist.
